text: You're at the doctor's, feeling unwell, wanting to see them. The receptionist hands you the clipboard. Again. You want this done, quickly.
You take the board, full of questions you've answered before. It feels inefficient. In this digital age, surely a faster, more secure way exists?
Your first thought: it’s cheap, or doctors are slow. You imagine sleek tablets, instantly updating records. Why this outdated relic?
But the clipboard isn't a flaw, it's a feature. It's a crucial buffer. You review data before it enters any digital system, preventing errors, ensuring accuracy.
This analog step provides legal clarity. Your signature on paper confirms consent and data accuracy. It creates an undeniable record, protecting you and the clinic.
So next time you’re handed that clipboard, you’ll still want to speed through it. But you’ll see it for what it truly is: a quiet, reliable cog, securing your sensitive information.
